blockers.b3d_human_ground_truth: B3D (jnc*) is scored on automatic ground truth from the same detector family as Tetris and the reference, so its results are provisional until the human-verified tracks of R1.O1 are passed with --gt-root. Provisional here: B3D1, B3D2, B3D3, B3D4.
leap_run_caveats: LEAP's native results and pseudo-labels for these runs are not on ace (possibly on another host's local /data), so LEAP's own ground-truth variants, class ids, and both true ends (start and end) of each of its ambiguous objects cannot be recovered.
The detector, DETECT_CLASSES, and flags of the LEAP runs are unknown.

B3D motion-pattern libraries may have been built from the 29-fps copies in LEAP/data/videos/jnc*, which would explain LEAP's long B3D intervals (about 3.5x the reference track length); unverified, and the libraries are not on ace.

Whether LEAP's empty exports (diagnostics leap_unwrap.empty_export_videos) are genuine empty outputs or failed runs is unknown; diagnostics leap_excluding_empty_exports rescores LEAP without those clips.
LEAP's runtime is inference_total - decode per video (evaluation/p140_otif_transform.py), so it excludes decoding and includes the JPEG writes of inference.py and the JSON writes of main.py.

On B3D3 (jnc6), LEAP's reid stage takes 159.1 s of its 174.4 s inference total (/sota-results/jnc6/leap_jnc6.csv), against totals of 21.0-26.9 s on the other B3D cameras, so Tetris-over-LEAP ratios on B3D3 reflect that outlier.
blockers.per_class_queries: LEAP's paper scores car, truck, and bus separately. No output or ground truth here has a class: the Tetris and reference detectors are single-class, tracking.jsonl rows are [track_id, x1, y1, x2, y2], OTIF labels every box car, LEAP's export labels every box car, and the ground truth has no truck or bus labels. Per-class queries need per-class ground truth, per-class Tetris and OTIF outputs (new GPU runs), and LEAP's native per-class results, which are not on ace. Only class-agnostic queries are scored.

aggregation.acc_leap: 1 - mape_leap, LEAP's ACC on unpadded frames
aggregation.mape_leap: mean over frames of |p - g| / g (g > 0), 0 (g = p = 0), 1 (g = 0 < p); not clipped
aggregation.mape_pos: mean |p - g| / g over frames with g > 0
aggregation.zero_fp_rate: share of g = 0 frames with p > 0

baselines.median: the ground-truth variant's lower median count on every frame (uses the ground truth)
baselines.one: 1 on every frame (every frame positive; a random top-k ranking)
baselines.use: datasets[*].baselines; a cell is trivial when the best of them meets its bound, and a query is non-informative on a dataset when one is at least as accurate as the reference

method.clip_length: rows of the reference pipeline's 002_naive/detection.jsonl, checked against the video frame count
method.counts: distinct track ids per frame of tracking.jsonl; missing frames count 0; frames >= clip length dropped

variants.moving: LEAP's pseudo_tuple: last - first >= 15 frames and first/last box centers >= 50 px apart, counted on [first, last); centers as data_prepare.py computes them from MOT left = x1 and width = x2 - x1: int((int(x1) + int(x1) + int(x2 - x1)) / 2), likewise for y (sensitivity; favours LEAP, which drops stopped vehicles itself)

method.lag_diagnostic: median per-clip Pearson correlation of counts with ground truth all, system frame f vs ground-truth frame f + lag, lag in [-15, 15]; warn when the best lag is nonzero and gains more than 0.05
method.leap_moving_fps_note: LEAP configs set fps 15 for every dataset but caldot2.yaml, which has no fps key; 15 is used

operating_points.granularity: topk_paper is a mean of multiples of 1/k = 0.1 over draws
operating_points.leap_ambiguity_dependent: cell.leap_ambiguity_dependent: leap and leap_ambiguous_dropped disagree on meeting the bound; quote both
operating_points.leap_fit: bound = LEAP's best accuracy per dataset; a bound at or below a constant answer's accuracy (for example <= 0) is flagged trivial
operating_points.rounding: bounds and selection use unrounded accuracies; JSON values are rounded to 4 decimals
operating_points.trivial: cell.trivial: the best constant answer (cell.trivial_baseline) meets the bound
operating_points.undefined: datasets whose reference accuracy is not positive are skipped per query

selection.degenerate: when every ground-truth frame is positive (ground_truth_summary.all_frames_positive, as on B3D), the constant answer one scores F1 1.0 and every cell is trivial
selection.f1: 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN), presence = count >= 1; null when no frame is positive on either side
selection.f1_leap_code: TP forced to >= 1, recall and precision rounded to 4 decimals before F1 (evaluate.py)

method.skipped_queries: Query-3 (distinct-id counts) and Query-4 (aggregation_query_2) are not queries in LEAP's paper

systems.leap: corrected SOTA cache (p140 unwrap); ambiguous full-span objects kept whole (upper bound)
systems.leap_ambiguous_dropped: LEAP without unwrap.json's ambiguous_full_span_objects (lower bound); LEAP's throughput, no HOTA

tie_draws.rule: numpy default_rng(seed) per configuration; draw r breaks ties by the r-th vector of uniform keys over the frames it can return; topk_paper_min/max over draws

topk.ties_at_cutoff: frames whose count equals that of the last frame returned in pooled order, accepted and suppressed frames included
topk.topk_leap_code: evaluate.py top_k_query_1 over pooled arrays with argsort(kind=stable); clusters may chain across clip boundaries; prediction clusters valued with ground-truth counts
topk.topk_leap_code_default_sort: the same with numpy's default argsort, as evaluate.py calls it
topk.topk_paper: mean over tie draws of the share of the system's returned frames with ground-truth count >= tau, over k; the system greedily returns its k highest-count frames >= separation apart (clips separated by a gap), never a frame where its count is 0; tau = min ground-truth count of the ground truth's k such frames (ties by pooled order; ground_truth_summary.tau_min/max_over_draws show it under random ties)
topk.topk_paper_pooled_order: the earlier deterministic score: ties by pooled order, zero-count frames returnable

method.unit: one pooled sequence per dataset: test clips concatenated in teNN order, start 0, end = pooled frames, no padding
